title: Accuracy failure in reduction kernel
body: I minimized an accuracy failure from a PyTorch Triton-pin update into PyTorch and Triton reproducers. The kernel adds fp16 inputs, converts to fp32, reduces across one dimension, subtracts the reduction, and produces output that does not match the equivalent eager PyTorch computation. I am running PyTorch 2.2.0a0+git9530e5e with CUDA 12.1 on an NVIDIA A10G. I also see reduction-test failures when adding two specific blocked layouts to test_reduce_layouts.

symptoms_visible: The Triton reduction kernel produces output that does not match the equivalent eager PyTorch add, fp32 reduction, and subtraction.
Two additional blocked layouts also produce failures when I add them to test_reduce_layouts.
N0.label: N0 reduction accuracy failure reported

symptoms_visible: The reduction accuracy failure occurs when the added layouts are used as source layouts.
N1.label: N1 source-layout placement clarified

symptoms_visible: The original PyTorch reproducer still produces an accuracy mismatch.
N2_x.label: N2_x malformed-layout explanation aftermath

symptoms_visible: The updated standalone kernel comparison still shows Triton output differing from the equivalent eager PyTorch result.
N2.label: N2 portable accuracy reproducer supplied

symptoms_visible: The reduced compiler reproducer gives the wrong result when the shared-memory load is vectorized.
Removing the relevant layout conversion or removing the reduction masks makes the reduced reproducer return the expected result.
N3.label: N3 compiler-level reproducer isolated

symptoms_visible: The failing IR-to-PTX path loads vectorized half values from shared memory without producing the required float conversions, while the working variant returns the expected result.
N4.label: N4 LLVM lowering defect identified

symptoms_visible: Maintainers report that the LLVM correction has been integrated and that the reduction-layout tests no longer reproduce another failure; I have not reported a retest of the integrated build on my original workload.
N_terminal.label: terminal fix integrated without reporter retest

question_patterns: Where in test_reduce_layouts did you add those layouts?
Were those layouts added as source layouts, destination layouts, or both?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I meant adding them to the list of src_layouts, because that is the encoding used for the reduce operation.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: I only added them as destination layouts after the reduction; they are never used as the reduce input encoding.
I added them to both lists, but the failure is still present when they are used only as source layouts.

edges.comment: From c4-c6: participant3 first tested a different placement, and the reporter clarified that the layouts belonged in src_layouts. This edge describes the reporter's test setup only.

solution.intent: Treat the reported reduction failure as malformed layout input because the supplied layouts request eight warps while the test launches four, and add a verifier to reject them.
solution.concrete_example: Reject these two test layouts because warpsPerCTA=[8,1] requires eight warps but the test is configured for four; add compiler verification for that mismatch.

edges.comment: From c10-c12: participant3 and participant1 correctly found that the two added test layouts were illegal for a four-warp launch, but the reporter immediately confirmed that the independent PyTorch reproducer still failed. Rejecting those layouts is useful validation work but does not resolve the opening accuracy bug.

question_patterns: Can you provide an updated reproducer that works across current PyTorch versions?
Can you make the accuracy failure directly compare the kernel output with an eager reference without relying on torch.compile or the original stored inputs?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I made an updated reproducer that does not call torch.compile. It launches the Triton kernel directly and compares its output against the equivalent PyTorch eager code, so it should work with more PyTorch versions. I also removed the recently added participant9_meta argument when it caused a version mismatch for another tester.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The direct kernel output matches eager PyTorch; the mismatch only occurs inside torch.compile with the original hard-coded storage.
The same direct comparison reproduces the mismatch after removing one version-specific launch metadata argument.

edges.comment: From c14-c20: maintainers could not reliably run the original environment-dependent script, so the reporter supplied a direct kernel-versus-eager comparison and edited out recent launch metadata. Participant5 then reproduced it, but that maintainer's setup is not merged into the reporter's own system state.

question_patterns: Can you reduce this to a compiler-level reproducer and show where the generated output first differs?
Can you compare a failing reduced case with a nearby working variant and share the relevant generated instructions?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I reduced it to a TTGIR reproducer. In the failing output I see a vectorized shared-memory instruction, `ld.shared.v4.b16 {%f1, %f2, %f3, %f4}`, feeding float registers. Removing the convert_layout operation or removing the reduction masks makes the output correct because that shared-memory load is no longer vectorized.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The reduced compiler input produces identical IR and PTX for the working and failing cases; the first difference only appears in the runtime input data.
A different harmless source edit prevents vectorization and makes the reduced case work, while the failing case still emits the same vectorized shared-memory instruction.

edges.comment: From c21-c30: the reporter independently reduced the case and reported raw TTGIR/PTX behavior. The conclusion that LLVM's NVPTX lowering is responsible is intentionally not placed in this measurement answer.

question_patterns: Can you share the complete IR and PTX for both sides of the failing and working snippets?
Please provide the full compiler outputs for the reduced failing case and its working variant.
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: Here are the full failing PTX and LLIR files, and the full working PTX and LLIR files.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The complete files show that the incorrect instruction is already present in the input IR before LLVM processes it.
The full files contain the same failing and working instruction sequences, with only symbol names and temporary numbering changed.

edges.comment: From c31-c33: participant7 requested complete files, the reporter attached the four raw outputs, and then the reporter independently identified that v8f16 was marked legal without a corresponding load-extension action. That unprompted diagnosis is recorded in N4.volunteered_info rather than being leaked through the question.

solution.intent: Correct LLVM's NVPTX lowering for vector-of-eight fp16 loads, integrate the corrected LLVM into Triton, and ask the reporter to retest the original reduction workload before declaring the user-visible issue resolved.
solution.concrete_example: Add the missing load-extension handling for the legal v8f16 type so shared-memory half values are loaded as halves and explicitly converted to f32, then update Triton's integrated LLVM and have the reporter rerun the direct kernel-versus-eager reproducer.
solution.inference_hint: The complete evidence shows that LLVM's NVPTX backend combined a load of <8 x half> followed by fpext into vectorized shared-memory loads that did not perform the required half-to-float extension. The corrected output loads packed half values and emits explicit f16-to-f32 conversions. This interpretation is grounded in the reporter's files and the maintainers' post-patch code-generation inspection.

edges.comment: From c33-c38: the reporter identified and submitted the LLVM-side correction; participant7 inspected the corrected generated code; participant3 reported no remaining test_reduce_layouts failures; participant1 recorded that the corrected LLVM integration was merged. No affected reporter subsequently confirmed the original workload, so the terminal state records integration without claiming user verification.

satisfaction_conditions: Must identify the final accepted root cause: LLVM NVPTX treated v8f16 as a legal type but lacked the corresponding load-extension action, allowing vectorized shared-memory half loads to reach float registers without the required fp16-to-fp32 conversion.

The diagnosis must be grounded in the reduced TTGIR, the failing and working LLIR/PTX pairs, and the observed vectorized shared-memory load behavior rather than inferred from floating-point reduction error alone.
Must not treat rejecting the two eight-warp layouts as the complete fix: those layouts were malformed for the four-warp test, but the independent PyTorch kernel-versus-eager reproducer still failed.
The fix must correct the LLVM NVPTX vector-half load-extension path and be integrated into Triton; merely changing reduction layouts or masking vectorization is not the final resolution.

Must ask the reporter to rerun the original direct accuracy reproducer on a build containing the integrated correction, and must not claim user-visible resolution because the thread contains no affected-user retest after integration.

persona_hint.experience_level: Compiler and PyTorch developer with strong CUDA, Triton IR, LLVM IR, and PTX expertise; capable of minimizing generated kernels, comparing eager references, and isolating backend lowering defects.
persona_hint.communication_style: Technical, concise, and collaborative; supplies complete reproducers and compiler artifacts, corrects earlier hypotheses openly, and independently narrows failures across compiler stages.
